_source: English translation of analisi/2026-11-03_eventi_descrizione.md (Notion: 'Gli eventi Orsi: cosa succede, come riconoscerli, durata, strumenti'). Names are the exact VU-Tapis step classes (outputs/orsi/LONG/control/totale/distributions/steps_distribution.csv); left/right variants are merged into the class shown.
scene: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (da Vinci), endoscopic view from above into the pelvis of a patient in steep Trendelenburg. Typical instruments: monopolar curved scissors (right of image; cut and coagulate, white smoke), bipolar grasper (left; thin tips), ProGrasp/Cadiere grasper (4th arm; wide fenestrated jaws; pulls bladder, vesicles, catheter), large needle drivers holding a silver curved needle with suture during stitching. Assistant tools: laparoscopic clip appliers (small silver metal clips or purple/green plastic Hem-o-lok clips), suction, endobag introducer.

events.name: Port_placement
events.what: A trocar (port) is pushed through the abdominal wall.
events.timestamp: when the obturator tip perforates the wall
events.cues: View of the inner abdominal wall (pink-white). A conical or bladed tip tents the wall inward, punctures it, then the trocar cylinder appears. No robotic instruments active yet.

events.name: Instrument_insertion
events.what: A robotic instrument enters the abdomen at the start of surgery.
events.timestamp: when the instrument tip enters the field of view or appears in the trocar opening
events.cues: Almost static scene (abdominal wall, bowel or fat in the distance); a dark metal tip appears from an image border or a circular hole and advances to the centre. 2-3 instruments arrive a few seconds apart.

events.name: Adhesion_removal
events.what: Adhesions (bands of tissue attaching bowel/sigmoid to the wall or pelvis) are freed to make working space.
events.timestamp: first cut or first coagulation of the adhesion
events.cues: Whitish taut bands or veils between shiny pink bowel loops and the wall, cut by the scissors, often with a little smoke. Different from the peritoneal incision, which is high above the bladder.

events.name: Incision_peritoneum_-_right
events.what: The peritoneum is incised laterally (right and left side) to detach the bladder from the anterior wall and enter the space of Retzius.
events.timestamp: first scissor cut on each side (usually two events, ~5 min apart)
events.cues: High, wide view of the anterior abdominal wall with whitish vertical umbilical folds. Scissors make the first cut in a smooth shiny veil; yellow spongy areolar fat appears behind. ProGrasp pulls the peritoneum down.

events.name: Incision_of_the_fascia_-_left
events.what: With the prostate exposed in the centre, the endopelvic fascia on the LEFT side of the prostate is opened.
events.timestamp: first cut or traction of the left fascia
events.cues: Prostate as a pinkish/orange bulge in the centre, partly cleared of yellow fat. On its side a shiny whitish sheet (fascia) is incised, revealing red fibres of the levator ani muscle beneath.

events.name: Placement_stitch_for_bladder_stretch
events.what: A stitch is passed through the bladder wall and pulled up to stretch the bladder neck.
events.timestamp: when the needle enters the tissue
events.cues: FIRST needle of the surgery: a silver curved needle in a blunt-tipped needle driver pierces the bladder dome (flesh-pink, top centre); then the thread is pulled up and the bladder tents upward.

events.name: Start_dissection
events.what: Separation between bladder and prostate begins at the bladder neck.
events.timestamp: first cut or coagulation of the scissors on the bladder neck
events.cues: Bladder held up by the stitch, prostate below. Scissors work on the horizontal border between them, with coagulation smoke and blanching tissue.

events.name: Visualisation_of_urethra_opening
events.what: Opening the anterior bladder neck exposes the urethra and the catheter inside it.
events.timestamp: first frame in which the catheter is visible in the opening
events.cues: A smooth, uniform, light-coloured tube (catheter: whitish, yellowish or orange) appears inside the cut red tissue and becomes more visible in the next seconds.

events.name: Grasping_catheter_tip
events.what: A robotic grasper grabs the catheter tip and pulls it up toward the abdominal wall, using it as a handle to lift the prostate.
events.timestamp: when the grasper jaws close on the catheter
events.cues: The light catheter tube is grasped and pulled upward; its tip leaves the opening and stays suspended at the top of the image. ~15 s after the catheter becomes visible.

events.name: Continue_posterior_dissection
events.what: With the catheter pulled up, the posterior bladder neck is cut to fully separate bladder from prostate.
events.timestamp: first cut after the catheter traction
events.cues: Catheter suspended at the top; scissors work below it, deep, on red and white tissue with smoke; bladder-neck fibres visible.

events.name: Identify_and_dissect_vas_deferens_-_right
events.what: Behind the bladder neck a vas deferens is isolated (left or right).
events.timestamp: when a vas deferens is first grasped or dissected, and again at each change of side
events.cues: Deep in the centre a firm, white, cylindrical cord (pencil-sized) wrapped in loose tissue; the grasper holds it and scissors free it.

events.name: Clip_or_coagulate_vas_deferens_-_right
events.what: The vas deferens is closed with a clip (then cut) or coagulated.
events.timestamp: when the clip closes or coagulation starts
events.cues: On the white cord a clip appears (Hem-o-lok purple/green plastic or metal) or the tissue blanches with smoke; then scissors cut and the two stumps separate. ~30 s after the vas dissection.

events.name: Identification_and_clipping_of_SV_arteries_-_right
events.what: The seminal vesicles are freed; their small arteries are closed with metal clips and cut. One event PER CLIP.
events.timestamp: each time a clip closes on the tissue
events.cues: Seminal vesicles are whitish-yellow, lobulated, sausage-like structures next to the vasa. A straight laparoscopic applier places a small shiny silver clip; clips accumulate over time (about one every 30 s, ~8 per surgery).

events.name: Lift_both_seminal_vesicles
events.phase: Posterior dissection between prostate and rectum
events.what: Both seminal vesicles are grasped and lifted to expose the Denonvilliers fascia beneath.
events.timestamp: first grasp with the intent of lifting them
events.cues: ProGrasp holds the vesicles (or cut vasa) and pulls them up and forward; a shiny whitish plane opens below.

events.name: Incision_of_Denonvilliers_fascia
events.phase: Posterior dissection between prostate and rectum
events.what: The Denonvilliers fascia (between prostate and rectum) is incised.
events.timestamp: first cut, usually ~12 s after lifting the vesicles
events.cues: Below the lifted vesicles a pearly-white horizontal sheet is cut transversally, opening a space with loose tissue and yellow fat; the smooth pink rectum may be seen in the depth.

events.name: Start_dissection_and_cutting_right_pedicle
events.what: Lateral detachment of the prostate begins by cutting the prostatic pedicle (its vascular bundle) on one side, then the other.
events.timestamp: first handling or cut of the pedicle on each side
events.cues: Prostate pulled sideways; scissors work on its flank on red vascular tissue, often without coagulation (nerve sparing). Clips follow shortly.

events.name: Metal_clip_on_right_pedicle
events.what: Pedicle vessels are closed with clips before cutting, one at a time, along the prostate flank (both sides, metal or Hem-o-lok). One event PER CLIP.
events.timestamp: each time a clip closes on the tissue
events.cues: Small silver metal clips or purple/green V-shaped plastic Hem-o-lok clips applied by a straight applier from above or the side; a row of clips builds up along the prostate flank; scissors cut between clip and prostate after each one. About one every ~37 s, ~13 per surgery.

events.name: Start_dissection_DVC
events.what: Division of the dorsal venous complex (veins over the prostatic apex) begins.
events.timestamp: first scissor cut into the DVC
events.cues: View back to the front/top, on the prostatic apex where it narrows toward the urethra. Scissors cut thick, dark, vascular tissue; possible dark venous bleeding.

events.name: Stitch_in_DVC_before_apical_dissection
events.what: A stitch is passed through the DVC to ligate it before cutting the apex.
events.timestamp: when the needle enters the DVC tissue
events.cues: A curved needle with thread reappears, high on the prostatic apex, crossing the tissue side to side; knot tying or thread traction follows.

events.name: Transection_of_the_urethra
events.what: The urethra is completely cut at the prostatic apex, freeing the prostate.
events.timestamp: first cut into the urethra
events.cues: Low in the centre a muscular tube (urethra) with the light catheter inside; scissors cut it, usually WITHOUT smoke, and the catheter becomes visible in the opening.

events.name: Prostate_bagging
events.what: The detached prostate is placed into a plastic retrieval bag (endobag).
events.timestamp: when the endobag introducer enters the field of view
events.cues: A rod enters from a trocar and opens a clear plastic bag with a rim ring, unlike any tissue; instruments push the oval pink-white prostate inside.

events.name: Tighten_endobag
events.what: The bag containing the prostate is closed by pulling its drawstring.
events.timestamp: when the bag is completely closed
events.cues: The clear bag closes like a purse into a bundle with a string coming out, then is moved aside. ~20 s after bagging.

events.name: Stitch_of_posterior_reconstruction
events.what: A stitch in the residual Denonvilliers fascia below bladder neck and urethra reconstructs the posterior plane (Rocco stitch) before the anastomosis.
events.timestamp: each time the needle enters the fascia
events.cues: Needle with thread deep below the urethral opening, taking whitish tissue at the bottom of the pelvis; the prostate is gone and the scene looks emptier.

events.name: Stitch_in_bladder
events.what: First stitch in the bladder neck to sew the bladder to the urethra (anastomosis). Only the first bladder stitch is an event.
events.timestamp: when the needle enters the bladder neck
events.cues: Needle with thread passes through the edge of the bladder opening (thick pink tissue, top); urethra with catheter below; the bladder neck is brought toward the urethra. Usually barbed (V-Loc) or double-armed suture.

events.name: V-lock
events.what: The barbed suture is secured by passing the needle through the small loop at the end of the V-Loc thread.
events.timestamp: when the needle passes through the loop
events.cues: Close-up of a coloured (green or purple) thread with a small eyelet; the needle driver threads the needle through the eyelet and pulls. Near the end of the anastomosis, ~20 s before the needles are cut.

events.name: Leak_test
events.what: The bladder is filled with water through the catheter to check the anastomosis is watertight.
events.timestamp: when the bladder neck starts to inflate
events.cues: Static view on the finished anastomosis; the bladder slowly inflates and one looks for clear fluid leaking from the suture line; instruments almost still, suction may be ready.

events.name: Cutting_the_needles
events.what: After suturing, the threads are cut to detach the needles.
events.timestamp: when the scissors cut the thread
events.cues: Scissors (or a needle driver with blade) close on a taut thread and the needle with a piece of thread is freed; often two cuts ~12 s apart.

events.name: Removing_needles
events.what: The cut needles are taken out of the abdomen.
events.timestamp: LAST frame in which the grasper holding the needle is visible
events.cues: A grasper (often the assistant's laparoscopic one) holds a needle with a bit of thread and withdraws toward an image border until it disappears; usually 2 per surgery ~15 s apart, ~7 s after cutting.

events.name: Insert_hemostatic_agens
events.what: A haemostatic agent (gel, absorbable gauze) or a gauze is inserted to stop bleeding or dry the field.
events.timestamp: when the agent or gauze enters the field of view
events.cues: A grasper brings in white material (rectangular gauze, fibrous or gelatinous material), contrasting with red tissue, placed on a bleeding area.

events.name: Endobag_removal
events.what: The bag with the prostate is extracted.
events.timestamp: when the endobag string is grasped for extraction, or the grasper holding it enters
events.cues: The light bag bundle is seen again; a grasper takes its string and pulls it toward a trocar; the bag slides out.

events.name: Drain_placement
events.what: A drain tube is placed in the pelvis.
events.timestamp: when the drain enters the field of view
events.cues: A soft transparent or white tube with side holes is pushed in by a grasper and laid at the bottom of the pelvis; almost always the last event.

events.name: Removal_of_robotic_instruments
events.phase: any (instrument swaps) and end of surgery
events.what: A robotic instrument leaves the abdomen: definitively at the end, or during an instrument swap (e.g. scissors to needle driver).
events.timestamp: LAST frame in which the instrument tip is visible (when it leaves the field of view)
events.cues: An instrument retracts in a straight line toward the image border or into the trocar and disappears; the scene stays without it for a few seconds. At the end 3-4 leave in sequence. Instruments that only move back without leaving do NOT count.
